summary: The SDK 2.3 migration does what it claims. Using my own harness (an SDK 1.30 client in a separate environment, a loopback fixture backend, stdio, SSE and an installed wheel outside the checkout) the five tool wire schemas and descriptions are byte-identical to the pre-migration v1 server's; invalid arguments produced zero backend requests; backend bearer and identifying headers are correct; execution errors are sanitized; a missing jsonschema fails closed; the wheel contains all modules and its console entry works; the hash-verified binary-only install is clean. CloudBank make check reproduced the author's full-suite totals exactly. One note-level security finding: the SSE listener, now loopback-only, accepts any Host and Origin header, so it has no DNS-rebinding guard (f1, follow-up queued). It is not a regression: the base bound every interface, and its SSE route returned HTTP 500 under SDK 1.30. Error-envelope semantics changed in two small ways (f2). The root suite's author totals could not be reproduced without nested repos (f4).

findings.description: The SSE transport has no DNS-rebinding or Origin protection. build_sse_app constructs SseServerTransport('/messages/') with no security_settings, so a browser page that rebinds a hostname to 127.0.0.1 could open /sse and /messages/ on the default loopback listener and call the read-only tools with the connector's backend bearer token. Loopback-by-default (the documented control) stops network peers, not browser-mediated access. The migration did not introduce this: the base bound all interfaces, and its SSE route did not work at all. The README's authenticated-gateway guidance covers external deployments only.
findings.evidence: curl -H 'Host: evil.example.com' -H 'Origin: http://evil.example.com' http://127.0.0.1:18773/sse -> 200 (also 200 with Host 127.0.0.1:18773 and the foreign Origin). connector/server.py build_sse_app: SseServerTransport('/messages/'); mcp.server.sse.SseServerTransport.__init__(self, endpoint, security_settings=None, max_request_body_size=4194304) accepts mcp.server.transport_security.TransportSecuritySettings.
findings.correction: Pass TransportSecuritySettings(enable_dns_rebinding_protection=True, allowed_hosts=[loopback names with port], allowed_origins=[...]) for the loopback default, make --host deployments extend the allow-list explicitly, add a test that a foreign Host/Origin gets 4xx, and document it. Queued as connector-sse-dns-rebinding-guard.

findings.description: Error-envelope semantics changed slightly for clients. An unknown tool now returns isError:true (v1 server: isError:false with the same 'ERROR: Unknown tool' text), and argument-validation failures now read 'TOOL_VALIDATION_ERROR: <msg> (path: ...)' instead of the SDK 1.30 text 'Input validation error: <msg>'. Both are consistent with the README ('existing error prefixes and isError: true') and are arguably more correct, and the five tool schemas are unchanged, but a consumer that matched the old text or relied on isError:false for unknown tools will notice. The migration doc's 'retain' wording slightly understates this.
findings.evidence: Same SDK 1.30 client against base and target: base nonexistent -> isError False; target -> isError True. base aurora_get_ethics_log {limit:0} -> 'Input validation error: 0 is less than the minimum of 1'; target -> 'TOOL_VALIDATION_ERROR: 0 is less than the minimum of 1 (path: limit)'. Probe output files base_stdio.json / v2_stdio.json in the reviewer scratchpad.
findings.correction: None required; note the changed envelope in the connector README on the next touch.
